issuer: the Registrar of Motor Vehicles of the Northern Territory (the Motor Vehicle Registry)
note: Read 2026-10-30 on the Northern Territory's legislation site. The Motor Vehicles Act 1949: a learner licence from 16 (s 9(4)), held at least 6 months before a licence is granted (s 10(1A)); a licence granted to someone who hasn't held one is provisional for 2 years if they are under 25 (s 10A): a full licence is had from 18 years 6 months, kept as 19 (a whole-year age, rounded up). The Motor Vehicles Regulations 1977 (in force at 18 November 2025), reg 8, make the prescribed period of a licence 10 years (s 104 lets the applicant ask for a shorter one, at least 12 months), held as the term. The Motor Vehicles (Fees and Charges) Regulations 2008 (in force at 1 July 2026) give the 10-year licence fee as 141 revenue units; the revenue unit's dollar value for 2026-27 is set under the Revenue Units Act 2009 and published by the Treasury, whose page refused the request behind a Cloudflare check, so the fee is null. NT.GOV.AU's licence pages refused the same way. The Territory's evidence of age card isn't held.

sources.title: Motor Vehicles Act 1949 (NT)
sources.said: The Registrar may grant a learner licence to an applicant who has attained the age of 16 years ... subsection (1) unless the person has held the learner licence for a continuous period of not less than 6 months immediately before the grant. ... the age of 25 years – 2 years;

sources.said: For the purposes of section 104(1) of the Act, the prescribed period is 10 years.
